test.name: Locality records guide should not route to search-wikipedia
test.description: User asks what genealogy records exist for a county and where they are held. SKILL.md's scope guard says a locality records-availability guide is locality-guide's job and must be declined without calling wikipedia_search. This is the sharpest boundary this skill has, because it pairs directly against positive test ut_search_wikipedia_001: the same place, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania, with the opposite correct verdict. A Wikipedia county article is genuinely half-useful background here, which is what makes the near-miss tempting. Restores coverage deleted in badb0b0c, whose test id 007 was reused for the historical-context boundary; from that commit until this one, two of the scope guard's three named branches had no negative test at all (#1662 deep dive, finding F5). The 'wikipedia-search-any' fixture is declared deliberately and is expected to go UNUSED — it registers wikipedia_search so the no-wiki-no-write clause can fire (#1788). Do not remove it as an unused fixture.

input.user_message: I'm researching ancestors in Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania. What genealogy records exist for this county and where can I find them?

negative.explanation: The user is asking which record sets exist for a county and which repositories hold them — a records-availability guide. search-wikipedia would return Wikipedia's general article on Schuylkill County (history, geography, population), which is background rather than an answer: it names no record set, no date coverage, and no repository. locality-guide consults place_search and collections_search to produce the records-availability report the question asks for.

judge_context: This is a grade_on_invariant negative test: PASS/FAIL is decided solely by the deterministic no-wiki-no-write validator (no wikipedia_search call, no .md summary saved). Routing and activation are NOT gated, because whether the model declines in place or hands off to locality-guide is a known-unstable model prior on genealogy-flavored prompts. The judge runs base-only and diagnostically here — its scores do not decide the outcome.

Ideal behavior is to decline the Wikipedia workflow and name locality-guide; note in your rationale whether the skill did so. Opening search-wikipedia and then declining is a routing imperfection worth noting, not an automatic failure.

The real harm this test guards against is search-wikipedia EXECUTING a wikipedia_search on the county and SAVING a summary, presenting encyclopedia background as an answer to a records-availability question. That is what the validator fails on.

Offering a Wikipedia summary of the county as an explicitly-labelled supplement AFTER naming locality-guide is acceptable as narration, but it must remain an offer: no wikipedia_search call and no saved file on this turn.

The wikipedia-search-any fixture is registered only so that invariant is falsifiable. A run that consumes it has already violated the scope guard; do not read its presence as a hint that a lookup is expected here.
